cases.surface_condition: marker splits a numeral token on the left from an immediately following unit/scale word on the right (e.g. NUM / million|percent|kilometers|miles|signatures|dollars)
cases.blamed_rule: Is the token immediately before the marker a numeral/date/percentage/name? If yes, bias score upward.
cases.proposed_rule: If left_last is NUM and right_first is a measurement/scale token in {million, billion, thousand, percent, %, k, m, mi, kilometer, kilometres, kilometer(s), kilometers, miles, signatures, signature, dollars, km, kg, m}, do NOT place this boundary in the topmost boost band; instead limit its boost to a mid-high band (target 40–75) so it is still considered but not preferred over safer lexical boundaries.

cases.surface_condition: marker immediately follows an organization/group name or extremist acronym (e.g., 'isil', 'daesh', 'isis') on the left and the right_first is a lowercased role/occupation noun like 'militant'/'member'/'official' that continues the predicate
cases.blamed_rule: Is the token immediately before the marker a numeral/date/percentage/name? If yes, bias score upward.
cases.proposed_rule: When left_last is a known organization token or acronym (examples: isil, daesh, isis, nato, un) and right_first is a continuation noun signaling a role/action (e.g., militant, member, official, leader, suspect, representative), reduce the immmediate top-band boost and place the cut into a milder boost band (target 40–75). This avoids over-prioritizing splits that separate a name/acronym from its predicate continuation, which frequently produce contradictions.

cases.surface_condition: marker occurs after the end of a quoted/named phrase or noun (e.g., report/discovery/emission/statement) and the right_first is a subordinating connector (because/that/which/while/when/as/since)
cases.blamed_rule: Left or right stretch that ends or begins with a lexical token translators typically render reliably will tend to raise the measured value.
cases.proposed_rule: If right_first is a subordinating continuation token in {because, that, which, who, when, while, as, since, due} AND the token immediately before the marker is one of {report, discovery, emission, statement, finding, claim, result}, demote this boundary into a mid band (target 30–70) instead of the top band. Quoted/named nominal phrases followed by subordinators often create contradictions with the remainder.

cases.surface_condition: marker falls immediately before the head noun 'language'/'languages' while the left side ends in degree/adverbial tokens (e.g., 'most', 'commonly') or adjectival cluster
cases.proposed_rule: If right_first is {language, languages} and the token immediately before the marker is a degree/adverb token in {most, commonly, generally, widely, commonly} or an adjectival form such as 'spoken', reduce the boost for that boundary into a mid band (target 30–70). This prevents over-prioritizing adjective-only fragments that rely on the following noun to be coherent.

cases.surface_condition: marker immediately follows a multi-word organization/agency name ending in tokens like 'service'/'department'/'agency' and the right_first is a verb token (does/is/does not) continuing the clause
cases.blamed_rule: Is the token immediately before the marker a numeral/date/percentage/name? If yes, bias score upward.
cases.proposed_rule: When left_last is an organizational head token in {service, department, agency, bureau, council, authority} or a proper-name token and right_first is a verb form like {does, do, is, was, are, were, does}, cap the upward name/org boost to a mid band (target 40–75). This avoids giving full top rank to boundaries that separate an organization name from its immediately continuing predicate (a frequent source of contradiction).

cases.surface_condition: marker falls between a numeric token on the left (NUM) and a continuing clause on the right that reinterprets the measurement (right_first lowercase, not a punctuation-terminated phrase)
cases.blamed_rule: Is the token immediately before the marker a numeral/date/percentage/name? If yes, bias score upward.
cases.proposed_rule: If left_last is NUM and the right_first is a common continuation token that typically carries the remainder of a measurement/clarification (e.g., it's, it, its, long, wide, tall) then reduce the numeric-driven top boost to a moderate band (target 40–75) rather than full top band. Preserve the numeral boost when the numeral is followed by punctuation (comma) or a capitalized named unit (safe anchors).

tie_fix: Ties arise when multiple markers match the same checklist heuristics and receive identical heuristic boosts; add a deterministic tiny offset (epsilon) that prefers markers whose right_first is a lexical token (not in {the,a,an,in,on,of,to,by,for}) to break ties instead of relying on positional tie-breakers.
summary: The scorer systematically over-prioritizes boundaries adjacent to numerals and named entities, giving them top-band scores even when splitting a number from its unit or an organization from its predicate — both common sources of contradiction. It also overvalues adjective-only fragments before head nouns like 'language' and quoted/named nominal phrases followed by subordinators. I propose mild, narrowly scoped downgrades (move from top band into a mid-high band 30–75) for these surface patterns so safe lexical cuts remain rewarded but risky splits are deprioritized.
